rules.text: A history storyteller's voice, not a classroom and not a Shorts-style "Today you'll build…" voice.
Now and then ask the viewer a direct question.
Light humour that young viewers get; never academic, never a lecture.
A paragraph may end with one short joke.
No English slang (the voice engine misreads it); light colloquial German is fine.
Open with a real question; never open with congratulations.
Address the viewer as "du" (lower case in running text), never "Sie"; never a lecturing "wir".
A joke never bends a fact.
End with an archaeological twist or "what is left today".
Numbers easy to hear: digits, only numbers from the linked facts; exact figures go on the on-screen card.
Never name a modern source (author, paper, museum, link). When records disagree, tell both in plain words: "Die Chronik der Trần berichtet…, die Geschichte der Yuan dagegen…".
Certainty words: legend → "der Legende nach"; debated → "manche Historiker meinen"; archaeology → "deutet darauf hin", never "beweist".
rules.from: vi.json R13 + GUIDE §6, rewritten for de (Plan 6)

rules.text: Open a new question every 60–90 seconds to keep the viewer.
At most 1–3 places per video where records disagree, the ones that matter most for the story.
Write natively for a viewer of this country who does not know Vietnam; never translate Vietnamese sentences.
Explain context a foreign viewer lacks only with the beat's own facts; otherwise say less.
Avoid long compound nouns; split them into two words or a short phrase.
